cache_credit: none; every prompt token is priced as a miss
order: single-turn, then multi-turn, then each memory category's prerequisites before its questions
first_request_floor: Local o200k_base tokens of the turn-0 message text plus the tools array, summed over the four arms, priced as peak cache misses, with no output and no chat template. The pinned memory instruction and core-memory text are not included. This is a lower bound on prompt spend if every slot ended after one request, not a forecast.
planning_upper: Peak prices, no cache credit. A single-turn slot is its local first-request tokens plus 500 output tokens. A trajectory turn is 6 requests at the greater of 1.5 times the mean prompt and the 95th percentile prompt of that family in the c47b186c bills, plus 900 output tokens. One extra force-quit turn (21 requests instead of 6) is added per memory category per arm. Sized to stay at or under $17 so the $20 cap is not the way the run is expected to end.
structural_cap: The same allowances with every trajectory turn taking the runner cap of 21 requests. That is the tail if the model never finishes a turn. It is not the planning number. The hard ceiling still stops the run.
frozen_plan: validation/cost.json is the plan the 0bf829c6 flight was sized and checked against, with the editors of that commit. This file is the same report recomputed with the editors above.
